description: Hello, we are two highschoolers looking for people with experience in web design/general coding!
summary: We developed a user-friendly interface that allows the general public to easily compare data from Earth locations with data from the Moon. Our website includes an interactive map that allows the user to select an Earth location and compare it to the Moon according to various characteristics. Additionally, we integrated a simple function using Jaccard similarity to evaluate the suitability of these locations based on user input. We also incorporated both well-known analogs and lesser-known locations; our overall goal was to take knowledge of existing Earth-Moon analogies and organize them into a simple, easily navigable format that allows for smooth comparisons and public access. With more time, our website could become a highly valuable tool; our next steps would be adding more locations and improving our similarity algorithm. Eventually, using this algorithm, one will be able to select an area on the map, view its data, and analyze its potential as a Moon analogy. This ability may someday be vital for scientists seeking to test equipment or astronauts hoping to train in a location akin to their destination.
details: We created a website, interactive map, and simple program to analyze several Earth locations as analogies to the Moon and possible sites for laboratory work, equipment testing, and astronaut training. We developed our website through Google Sites, Google Maps, and One Compiler; we wrote a basic algorithm using Python to numerically compare and contrast the Earth sites to our selected Moon site, Mons Mouton. Our project is unique because we do not have advanced coding or software skills; instead, we relied on our research and data interpretation abilities to complete the project. We were also able to finish this project without any AI. When selecting Earth sites similar to those on the Moon, we considered the qualities of elevation, rainfall, temperature, flatness, light exposure, life present, dirt texture, and atmospheric pressure. In the future, we would consider expanding our database to include more locations on Earth, as well as including lava tubes on the Moon for possible research areas. We would also like to look at Mars and its different requirements compared to the Moon for analogous Earth locations.
